description: PRESERVED DEFECT 1 at position 1: the report comes out COMPLETELY EMPTY - zero TRANREPT records, not even a header - and the job still returns 0. Four records are seeded, every one on card 0500024453765740, which is row 1 of app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt and carries XREF-ACCT-ID 00000000050, so no account break can confound the trace. Row 1 carries TRAN-PROC-TS (1:10) = 2021-12-31, strictly below WS-START-DATE under both ASCII and EBCDIC collation, and it trips the defect on the VERY FIRST iteration; rows 2-4 carry 2022-01-01, 2022-04-15 and 2022-07-06, all inside [2022-01-01, 2022-07-06] with two of them sitting exactly ON the inclusive boundaries, and they exist purely so that their COMPLETE ABSENCE from the output is observable. THE EMPTY REPORT FOLLOWS FROM TWO FACTS AND NEITHER ALONE IS ENOUGH. First, the inline PERFORM UNTIL that opens at app/cbl/CBTRN03C.cbl:170 and closes on END-PERFORM. at :206 is ONE COBOL sentence, and its terminating period sits on that END-PERFORM at :206 - not on the END-IF at :178, which is where a reader expects it - so NEXT SENTENCE at :177 transfers control to the first statement of the NEXT sentence, PERFORM 9000-TRANFILE-CLOSE. at :208. It ends the entire read loop; it does not skip a record. Second, 1120-WRITE-HEADERS (:324-341) is reachable on this path from exactly one place: :279, inside 1100-WRITE-TRANSACTION-REPORT under IF WS-FIRST-TIME = 'Y', and 1100 is itself performed only at :196, on the detail path. So when the FIRST record read is out of range the loop is over before 1100 has ever run, and the four-record header block - REPORT-NAME-HEADER, WS-BLANK-LINE, TRANSACTION-HEADER-1, TRANSACTION-HEADER-2 - is never written either. 1120-WRITE-DETAIL never runs. 1110-WRITE-PAGE-TOTALS and 1110-WRITE-GRAND-TOTALS never run because the end-of-file arm at :197-203 is never reached, and 1120-WRITE-ACCOUNT-TOTALS never runs because its only caller is :183, inside that same detail path. TRANREPT is created by 0100-REPTFILE-OPEN (:394-396), written to ZERO times, and closed by 9100-REPTFILE-CLOSE (:532-548) still holding nothing. THE UNWRITTEN STATE, invisible in the output and part of what this case means: WS-FIRST-TIME never leaves 'Y', because the only MOVE 'N' is at :276 inside the paragraph that never runs; WS-LINE-COUNTER stays 0; WS-PAGE-TOTAL, WS-ACCOUNT-TOTAL and WS-GRAND-TOTAL all stay 0 and not one of them is ever written; and WS-CURR-CARD-NUM stays the SPACES of :137, because the card-break block at :181-188 is inside the detail path. NO LOOKUP IS EVER PERFORMED: no keyed read against CARDXREF, none against TRANTYPE, none against TRANCATG. All three are opened at :163-165 and closed at :210-212 completely untouched, so this case exercises the open and close paths with no keyed access whatsoever - a shape it shares in the folder only with case08, case09 and case17, and it is the only one of those four that seeds SEVERAL fully resolvable in-range rows and still reads none of them, which is what makes the silence here evidence about the loop rather than about the input. The three files are nevertheless seeded precisely because the program OPENS them: an unseeded dataset would change the open outcome at :415, :433 or :451 and turn a silent empty report into an abend. GATES G20 AND G21 ARE SATISFIED VACUOUSLY: there is no 133-byte line to measure and no FILLER span to prove emitted, so the dataset-level expectation of zero rows at the 133 bytes app/jcl/TRANREPT.jcl:78 and app/proc/TRANREPT.prc:76 declare is the assertion, and the absence of any line is itself what is being asserted - a state no row-level expectation can describe, which is why expectedWrites and expectedFinalState are present and empty rather than omitted. THE MESSAGE LIST IS THE SHARPEST SIGNATURE IN THE FOLDER: exactly three lines. There is no DISPLAY TRAN-RECORD line, because :180 is on the detail path. There is no 'TRAN-AMT ' line and no 'WS-PAGE-TOTAL' line, because :198-199 are in the end-of-file arm. There is no INVALID line and no 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' line, because no lookup and no I/O error occurs. PRACTICE B5 GOVERNS: the empty report IS the expected result, inherited legacy behaviour deliberately preserved and never repaired. A corrected skip-and-continue would have read rows 2-4 and produced the four-record header block, three detail lines and then, at end of file, a page total, its trailing rule line and a grand total - ten records where this case expects none; the three in-range amounts sum to 2,713.44, which defect 2's end-of-file re-add of row 4 would have carried to 2,801.43 in both totals. Encoding any of that instead would be a behaviour change and a parity violation. This is the case in the folder most likely to be helpfully wrong: an implementation that writes the header block EAGERLY at job start rather than lazily from the first detail record produces exactly four records here and still passes every other case in the folder, and that divergence is what this case exists to catch. NEXT SENTENCE appears exactly ONCE in the whole COBOL corpus - this single site at :177 - and CBTRN03C contains ZERO GO TO statements, so it is the program's only non-structured control transfer. In production the defect is LATENT: the upstream EXEC PGM=SORT step pre-filters the range with INCLUDE COND=(TRAN-PROC-DT,GE,PARM-START-DATE,AND,TRAN-PROC-DT,LE,PARM-END-DATE) at app/jcl/TRANREPT.jcl:47-48, whose SYMNAMES at :41-44 resolve TRAN-PROC-DT to bytes 305-314 and pin the very range this case seeds, so an out-of-range record normally never reaches CBTRN03C at all; one is seeded deliberately to expose it. PRESERVED DEFECT 2 - the end-of-file re-add at :200-201 against a record area the failed READ left untouched - DOES NOT APPEAR HERE AT ALL, because the end-of-file arm is never reached: a useful negative signal separating the two defects, and the reason case12 and this case pin different message lists for the same single NEXT SENTENCE. Both of the program's two EVALUATE statements are exercised on their '00' arm and neither reaches WHEN OTHER, which is last in both (gate G30): '00' from 0550-DATEPARM-READ at :222-229, and '00' from the one successful TRANFILE read at :251-258. The TRANFILE '10' arm is NOT reached, because the loop ends before end of file, and that is exactly what distinguishes this case from case17, where an empty input reaches '10' on the first read and still produces nothing. The reporting range comes from the 80-byte DATEPARM record - line 15 of the skeleton at app/cbl/CORPT00C.cbl:117-121, right-truncated to the 21-byte WS-DATEPARM-RECORD at :122-125 - and never from a PARM, because app/jcl/TRANREPT.jcl:59 gives STEP10R none, so jobParameters is empty. Every seeded amount is TRAN-AMT PIC S9(09)V99 DISPLAY at bytes 133-143 of the 350-byte CVTRA05Y record: eleven bytes, ten plain digits and the sign overpunched into the TRAILING byte using {ABCDEFGHI for +0 through +9 and }JKLMNOPQR for -0 through -9, the convention app/data/ASCII/dailytran.txt carries - so 0000002507N is -250.75, 0000001254E is +125.45, 0000025000{ is +2500.00 and 0000000879I is +87.99, and the type and category keys 040002, 010001, 020002 and 070001 are all real rows of app/data/ASCII/trancatg.txt even though not one of them is ever looked up. Every amount is scale exactly 2, and ROUNDED appears zero times in CBTRN03C and zero times in any of the 28 programs, so a store truncates toward zero rather than rounding - but NO ARITHMETIC IS ACTUALLY PERFORMED IN THIS CASE, because every ADD in the program sits on a path that is never taken. The cross-reference rows are seeded from the 36-byte fixture UNPADDED, and the declared CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 normalisation is what widens them to the 50 bytes app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy declares, so the fixture's missing trailing FILLER PIC X(14) is padded at seeding time rather than hidden (gate G16, risk R-F). The code page is US-ASCII, stated explicitly rather than taken from the platform. RETURN-CODE is 0 because the program moves nothing to it: the job reports success while producing nothing, and that silence is the whole point. PROVENANCE (practice B12): every value here is STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of the COBOL, cross-checked against the byte layouts of CVTRA05Y, CVTRA07Y, CVACT03Y, CVTRA03Y and CVTRA04Y, the DD and DCB contracts of TRANREPT.jcl and TRANREPT.prc, and the real ASCII fixtures under app/data/ASCII - it is NEVER captured from an execution of the legacy COBOL, which AAP section 0.7.6 documents as impossible in this environment behind eight independently verified blockers, and that substitution of provenance alone is escalated as risk R-A rather than silently absorbed.
